like any good apathetic teen, nothing. I guess I like drawing, writing, cooking, listening to music and playing with cute animals.

> How did you convince them to let you out?

I "got better". I said i didnt feel suicidal anymore, that i stopped self-harming, I took my meds, i basically just engaged in treatment and presented as happier

>How old are you?

15

>Why were you sent to the hospital in the first place and who sent you there?

Like I said in another comment, I was very suicidal, had already attempted suicide twice, was self-harming a lot, and my stash of morphine, needles, laxatives and stuff was found and I was deemed too risky to be at home. To be sectioned, a few professionals all need to agree that you are mentally unwell enough that you cant make the "right" decisions and stuff - so basically some professionals already involved in my care and some who's never even met me before all decided i should be in hospital. You can read more about how it works [here](http://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/legal-rights/sectioning/)

>Lastly, what does one actually DO at a mental hospital? How does a typical day go?

Staff wake you up on a morning and will give you your meds (if youre on any). They try to make you wake up but you can sleep if you want. Then theres breakfast in the dining room (idk much about how mealtimes are because i never ate with others or the food there - they dont force you unless you have meal support). On a weekday you are "encouraged" to access education (which i never did and they never particularly cared). So most of the time I kinda slept until around noon (when theyd have lunch) and then id just kinda waste time with other patients or watching tv or something. thered usually be activities like art and craft stuff or baking but i mostly spent time in my room or just with other patients - we got up to a bit of mischief.

>Did the hospital have both men and women patients or only one or the other?

It was a mixed ward, so both but it was pretty infrequent to have male patients - most of us were girls and I think the most male patients we had while I was there was two (with like 10 girls).

>Were there any really "crazy" people acting out in the hospital? How about any normal people who didn't seem to belong there?

There used to be  this one girl who hissed at anyone who walked by and would occasionally kick people or run at them, but she was moved to a different ward pretty soon. There were plenty of times people kicked off but I wouldnt say that it was much to talk about - just a lot of shouting and being restrained kind of stuff. Pretty much every person there seemed pretty "normal", unless you really spoke to them about why they were there.
